correctness.rationale: Every binary five-point row set has affine rank exactly three or four and is equivalent to one of two explicitly specified representatives. Fully exhaustive finite local tables of size 56 and 4368 are independently evaluated with exact Bareiss and permutation determinant methods. The uniform quotient-projection lemma gives exactly (Q/2^r)^5 lifts for distinct local projected columns, proving all formulas for every d>=4. Maximizer translates are checked exhaustively; the second-moment Cauchy--Binet identity confirms global consistency. Independent external audit is not claimed.

originality.rationale: The dimension-four numeric distribution, maximal possible ±1 order-five determinant 48, and generic mean-square count are known and explicitly excluded from novelty. The assessed theorem is the closed all-dimensional Sylvester 5x5 magnitude distribution together with the affine quotient optimizer characterization. Relevant arXiv full texts, the 2008 ETNA full paper, published exact small-case censuses and targeted literature/published-finding corpus searches have not exhibited equivalent parameter-uniform coverage. Historical priority remains a bounded, explicit risk.
residual_risks: Brent--Osborn 2012 supplementary table directly includes all d=4 determinant magnitudes/multiplicities. These are acknowledged as prior data, not a new subtheorem.
An alternative known small Hadamard-minor incidence theorem, coding-design association scheme, or weight enumerator may imply the all-dimensional formulas without matching title or keywords.
Unrestricted literature priority is not proved by bounded searches; broader historical survey and independent validation are outstanding.

The four-by-four all-dimensional Walsh minor classification is a close method predecessor; the five-by-five classification is motivated by its distinct extremal 48 and fourth-dimensional affine span, but some proof components are similar.

value.rationale: Determines the complete discrete volume distribution of all five-observation Walsh Fourier masks, the exact singular percentage and the sharp maximum-volume sampling counts in every binary dimension, and gives an affine-geometric description of all optimizers. The limiting nontrivial four-atom law and all-dimensional formula extend finite case tables; they are a natural, usable calibration for Fourier interpolation and D-optimal sampling rather than arbitrary small-number recomputation.
